text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Tuesday.
- Defence Minister Gojko Susak travels to the United States for talks with his American counterpart William Perry. Croatia is also to buy American Bell helicopters for its army.
- Serb minority children will have an extracurricural programme in Serb language and literature in primary schools.
- Total workforce shrank by 7.1 percent in September compared to the same month last year.

- From January to September Croatia exported goods worth $3.2 billion, 9.1 percent less than in the same period last year. Import totalled $5.5 billion, down 2.8 percent. Germany and Italy remain the country's main trade partners.

- State oil company INA produced 792,690 tonnes of crude in the first nine months of 1996, only one percent les than planned and imported five percent less. September production totalled 83,480 tonnes of crude.
- Ministry of Tourism expects 4.4 million tourists in 1997 and 26.5 million overnight stays, 20 percent more than this year. It also expects to cash some 13 billion kuna from tourist trade.

- Heads of counties and town mayors earn between 4,000 and 8,000 kuna, while company managers earn 15 times more. July salaries for the latter ranged between 19,000 to 88,000 kuna, or between 5,500 and 25,000 German marks.
- Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic is paying a visit to Croatia to discuss further normalisation of relations.

- Commentary: European Union's regional approach to the countries of southeast Europe may not be to Croatia's liking, but the country could be condemned to remain a part of the Balkans, mostly because of its ties with Bosnia.

- Of 100 citizens, only one is a stock market expert, ten are following bourse activites because they are shareholders, and the rest have either no interest or have accidentaly found themselves in the whirl of privatisation. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
